answers.nudge:
## Conference trip expenses

| Category | Items | Total |
|---|---|---|
| **Travel** | Uber SF airport (48.20), Delta baggage fee (35.00), Uber hotel to venue (22.10) | **$105.30** |
| **Meals** | Chipotle (14.75), Starbucks (6.40), Dinner w/ team (143.50) | **$164.65** |
| **Lodging** | Hotel Marriott, 3 nights (612.00) | **$612.00** |
| **Other** | Notebook and pens (18.99) | **$18.99** |
| **Grand total** | 8 receipts | **$900.94** |

I checked the total two ways. The category subtotals and the line items both add up to $900.94.

**Judgment calls**
- **Baggage fee:** I put it under Travel because it's an airline charge. Some expense systems file it under "Airfare & fees", so check yours.
- **Notebook and pens:** I put these under Other as office supplies. If you used them for conference notes, you could also call them a business supply.

**Things that commonly get a report bounced**
- **Team dinner ($143.50):** Most policies want the attendee names and the business purpose. Some also cap the per-person amount. Add both now while you remember who was there.
- **Hotel ($612.00):** This works out to $204/night. Make sure you have the itemized folio, not just the card receipt. Taxes and fees are sometimes coded separately, and any incidentals such as parking, minibar or Wi-Fi may be non-reimbursable.
- **Meals:** The three meal receipts are across at least two days. If your company pays a per diem instead of actuals, the per diem rate may replace these amounts.
- **Uber rides:** Some policies require the trip receipt showing the route, not just the charge. Download them from the app.
- **Missing items:** The list has no airfare, return transportation from the hotel to the airport, or breakfasts. If those exist, add them before you submit. If you paid for the flight yourself, it will likely be the largest line item.

If you want, I can turn this into a CSV or a spreadsheet-ready expense report with date and vendor columns. I'd need the dates and payment methods for that.
